title: Writing a Short Letter as Elizabeth Bennet After Overhearing a Conversation
summary: Students work in small groups, imagining themselves as Elizabeth Bennet who has overheard a key conversation in the novel. They write individual letters, share them with a partner, and volunteers present theirs to the whole class.

title: Pride and Prejudice Section 4: Warm-Up, Story Summary and Reading for Gist
summary: This section guides students through a warmer discussion of the novel's events so far, reading a summary of the story, and then reading a literary extract to identify true and false statements about Mr Wickham and Mr Darcy.

title: Vocabulary from Context Practice and Letter Writing as the Late Mr Darcy
summary: Students complete sentences using vocabulary words, compare answers in pairs, then imagine they are the late Mr Darcy writing a letter to his son, sharing their letters with a partner and the class.

title: Pride and Prejudice Section 5: Story Summary, Reading for Gist and Detail
summary: This section includes a warmer discussion, a story summary reading with a comprehension question, and an extract-based reading activity with multiple choice questions followed by true or false statements for detailed comprehension.

title: Word Pronunciation Practice and Letter Writing as Elizabeth Bennet to Wickham
summary: Students practice the pronunciation of vocabulary words and generate example sentences with them, then imagine themselves as Elizabeth Bennet writing a letter to Mr Wickham, sharing drafts with a partner and the class.

title: Pride and Prejudice Section 6: Story Summary, Sequencing Events and Detailed Reading
summary: The section covers a warmer discussion, a story summary with a prediction question, sequencing events from an extract in correct order, and answering detailed comprehension questions about Elizabeth and Darcy's interaction.

title: Vocabulary Answer Key and Letter Writing as Mr Darcy Announcing News to His Aunt
summary: Students review vocabulary answers including words like valuable, period, and generous, then write a letter as Mr Darcy informing his aunt of recent news, sharing their writing with a partner and volunteering to read to the class.

title: As You Like It Introduction: About the Play, William Shakespeare and Initial Predictions
summary: Students introduce themselves with favourite book titles, learn about Shakespeare's play As You Like It and the author, predict the play's content, and explore vocabulary such as playwright, Globe Theatre, exile, and forbidden.
